title: smime-tree: encrypt_aes_cbc return type warrants a named struct
description:
Why this exists: smime_tree/src/encrypt.rs has #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)] on encrypt_aes_cbc, whose return type is Result<(AlgorithmIdentifierOwned, Vec<u8>, Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>), SmimeError>. The tuple has three elements with no names; callers use .0, .1, .2 indexing.

What goes wrong: the three elements of the tuple are (algorithm_id, encrypted_content, encrypted_key) — but the caller reading .0, .1, .2 at the call site has no documentation of which is which. Swapping any two elements in the tuple compiles fine but produces a subtle bug. The #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)] annotation acknowledges the problem without fixing it. A named struct with fields alg_id, encrypted_content, encrypted_cek makes the positions self-documenting and makes the swap a compile error.

Fix: define a private struct AesCbcEncryptResult { alg_id: AlgorithmIdentifierOwned, encrypted_content: Vec<u8>, encrypted_cek: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> } and return it from encrypt_aes_cbc. Remove the #[allow] annotation.
close_reason: P2 refactoring: the 3-tuple return from encrypt_aes_cbc is used in one place. Named struct adds a type definition for a single call site. Low priority.
